name: Community Care Network Next Gen (CCN NG)
value: Est. $700B IDIQ ceiling; $56.2B FY2027 community care account (+17%)
description: Next-generation VA community care MA-IDIQ (Solicitation 36C10G26R0003) for CCN Next Gen Medical, replacing current CCN regional contracts. Two new mechanisms enter that do not exist in current CCN: (1) value-based payments starting with lower-extremity joint replacement episodes, with at least three more VBP models added over the performance period; (2) utilization management requiring clinical decision support at the point of authorization. Corporate Experience gate is binary across three references: implementation, program management, and IT integration across multiple states — missing any one factor = Unacceptable. Forces teaming between healthcare payers and systems integrators. MOSA structure with No-Bid provision allows specialized firms to win bench positions and respond only to matching task orders.

description: Industry day held March 31, 2026. Draft strategy separates work into distinct contract lanes: PMO support, product support, and services support — plus Technical Integration, Product Management, and Human-Centered Design (HCD) carve-outs. There will be no prime systems integrator. Authority stays with the government. The Technical Integration contract performs traditional SI functions (architecture, engineering, integration design, system-level testing, release coordination) but does NOT own solution vendors, control execution, or have subcontracting authority. The HCD carve-out is a small focused team shaping workflows, usability, and requirements rather than owning delivery; likely driven by GAO oversight pressure and the widely cited 40/100 SUS score. Solutions (Oracle, Philips, etc.) and Services (deployment, support, etc.) operate independently with coordination through program governance, not contractual control. Key shifts from November 2025: DHA moved away from prime model due to OCI concerns; more willingness to accept risk in exchange for competition and flexibility; hosting no longer tied to OCI/OC3 — vendors can host in their own cloud if they meet performance/security/cost requirements. T1/T2 helpdesk scope stays with GSC provided by J6 (no changes). RFI close date: Aug 30, 2026.
sb_note: Multiple distinct lanes create new prime and sub opportunities. HCD carve-out is a small focused contract — potential SDVOSB/WOSB target. Services lane likely to include small business set-asides.

name: VA EHRM (Electronic Health Record Modernization)
description: VA's enterprise EHR modernization replacing VistA. Four Michigan sites went live April 11, 2026 (Detroit, Saginaw, Ann Arbor, Battle Creek) — the first wave of 13 sites planned for 2026 deployments (Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky, and Alaska to follow). Performance record is the primary driver of Congressional pressure: VA IG documented 826 major performance incidents since first go-live, GAO found only 13% of staff believe the system makes VA more efficient, and 58% believe it increased patient safety risks. FY2026: $3.4B allocated but 30% ($1.02B) withheld until July 1, 2026 pending VA conditions. Oracle exercised 3rd option period in 2025. Rep. Budzinski's 33-page discussion draft (March 2026) proposes a 2-year clock: if VA can't certify improvement and complete 2 new deployments, Oracle contract extensions would be restricted. Oracle facing reported 20-30% layoffs that could further strain EHRM staffing.

name: MHS GENESIS (DHMSM Bridge)
vendor: Leidos / Oracle Health (Cerner) / Accenture Federal Services / Henry Schein
description: DoD enterprise EHR deployed at 3,200+ locations serving 9.5M beneficiaries and 205,000 providers. Worldwide deployment completed March 2024. Leidos bridge is a planned/reported ~$1.4B sole-source extension; competition is delayed to 2028 at the earliest. The reported sole-source bridge has been justified by two factors: (1) documentation gaps — MHS GENESIS documentation lived inside Leidos's institutional knowledge, preventing competitive transition, and (2) the February 2024 Change Healthcare ransomware attack forced DHA to reassess documentation security. Oct 2025: $570M enterprise services task. UPDATE (March 31, 2026): HCDS Industry Day confirmed the MOSA follow-on will NOT use a prime SI model. The bridge-to-HCDS transition now routes through 5 distinct contract lanes (Technical Integration, Product Management, HCD, Solutions, Services) with no single vendor controlling the ecosystem. This is a fundamental shift from the Leidos sole-source model.
